citation.authors: Tahiri M, Johnsrud C, Steffensen IL

cited_by.title: Sea moss (Irish moss): health claims, iodine and heavy metals

record.population: Humans, experimental mammals and cells (scoping review of the additives carrageenan E407 and processed Eucheuma seaweed E407a)
record.finding: The most studied adverse effects of carrageenan on the intestines were inflammation, the gut microbiome, intestinal permeability, and cancer, metabolic and immune effects. Only five publications on carrageenan were in humans. The authors call for randomised trials of realistic dietary exposures.
record.note: About the food additive, not sea moss gel; it maps what is unknown and shows that human data are scarce. Counted as lab-level because most publications were in animals and cells.
